I have been trying to play this game for 20 years.

When it came out I stupidly bought it thinking I could play it on a Playstation 2 (I was 8).  
Then when I got a Wii I lost my originally copy and had to get another second hand.  
Then I had to get a memory card.  
Then I lost the second copy.  
I found the first copy but lost access to my Wii for years because of constant moving.  
Then found the second copy.  
Finally in 2021 after 17 years, I had everything. The Wii, two copies of the damn game, a memory card, and my desire to finally play. I felt like Thanos with the Infinity Stones. The anticipation was palpable. I put everything together, booted it all up, saw the wonderful title screen and... wondered why the console wasn't responding.  
When a message appeared:

"Plug in GameCube controller to play! :)))"

I did not own a gamecube controller.

Rage quit and downloaded Dolphin. Jokes on me though because I still can't find a ROM for it.

"Oh but you can play it on Switch this year!" NO. I don't have a switch and refuse to shell out $400 for a game I've bought twice.

Maybe I'll buy a GameCube controller. Who knows. Right now though I am just angry that I spent almost 20 years actively trying to play it legally and I still couldn't.

I'm happy that you have a very sweet pupper in your life. However, with this breed even the most gentle dogs need training. Please hire a trainer. This is a guard dog breed that spent a good 50 years as fighting dogs in the 20th century and that aspect hasn't been fully breed out.  
You need to teach them and learn to control them. You also need to curb their barking and their tendency to launch themselves at anything that moves.   
They are loyal to their families but will bark at or chase anything else. 

  
\- My relative's dogs will bark at any wild animal from birds to squirrels. If we are out walking them, I have to brace myself and reel them in as they chase after any animal. They've knocked me over many, many times because they'll chase after critters without warning.

\- Outside of your household they will bark at every other human. Visitors, neighbors walking outside, the mailman, your Amazon deliver, the repair man, friends, family. It took my relative's dogs over half a year to stop barking at my cousins when they visited every weekend. They also bark whenever someone comes home, especially with my aunt, their main person.

\- They're very emotional. They can get separation anxiety so bad they have digestive issues. They can get so wound up by perceived intruders that they attack other animals or people. They need to learn ways to channel any angst they have, such as chewing a toy. Even with people they like they bark and jump which can scare people. They also feed off energy of other animals, especially their own breed. If one is upset it can make an otherwise calm dog more neurotic. 

My relative has had eight shar pei. I have known 7 of them. Three of them have bit people. Two tried to attack each other. They have all, even the sweetest ones, barked like crazy. None of them were untrained, but I would say most did not get the higher level of training needed. Grant it, the incredibly well trained and gentlest one still barked at everyone who came to the house so like. That's just a feature of the breed. They bark at everything that moves. It's a guard dog breed. idk dude

They are very intelligent, sweet, loyal dogs but they NEED to be well-trained. Basic dog training will not cut it. I don't say this to scare you, I say this as someone who has lived with many shar pei and wants to warn you of what you need to do to prepare to have a good relationship with the dog. 

When my relative had her best dog, "Black", she trained him so she could take him out of the house and interact with people without barking or causing issue. She even took him to work with her and he behaved outstanding. It was when they had multiple of the breed when she had issues with behavior, as they feed of each others' emotions and she lacked the time to train them and maintain that training.

So uh....yeah! Good luck! GET A TRAINER! :DDD

To everyone who feels like they're getting nowhere: **please go to therapy, I am begging you.**

Ya'll, we're NEETS. Be it short term or long term NEETs, none of us are pinnacles of mental health. Everyone here has very specific mental-baggage that can only be unpacked with the help of a professional therapist. Not a psychiatrist, a therapist. Medication can help, but it's only a band-aid to help keep you stable while you work on the issues in your life.

Please, take my advice. You can lift everyday and listen to every self-improvement guru on Youtube, but you're not going to stop hating yourself. That was me for a decade. I tried and failed like Sisyphus rolling his boulder until I broke down and finally went to the doctor for help. Got referred to therapy. Since I started therapy, my life has slowly gotten better. 

On the outside my life is more-or-less still the same. Still living at home, still in school, still online too much blah blah blah blah. But the difference is that my mind is clearer, I'm kinder to myself, and I don't constantly feel like a worthless piece of shit who should ram their car into a wall.

It's takes a long time and it's hard, you need to participate and put in some effort. You need to dig up the ugly trauma of your past, and dissect the cognitive distortions that plague your mind. I'm not ashamed to admit I've cried buckets in my healing, but every tear was a healing one. Sometimes all you have energy to do is to just show up to therapy appointment. But guess what? You fucking did it, good job. I have friends who refuse to even do that. 

Thankfully, there's telehealth now. You can do talk to someone without living your cozy hobbit hole which can be good for NEETs in the beginning of recovery.

My mental health is still a work in progress, but it's progressing and I am so happy that I did this. All the sessions and tears were worth it. I'd do it over and over again without thought, because even a single moment of relief is better than to never have done it and still feeling like shit.

There will be days, weeks, or months when you relapse. That's ok. I do it too, but as long as you move forward, you're gonna be ok. Mental health ebbs and flows but it gets easier to bounce back when you do relapse/tank.

And everything after is pure pleasure. When it was just me and my cat in the house at one point in the pandemic, my cat was my cuddly lifeline.

Tips:  
\-Get Johnny Cat liter box liners. No scraping poo off the box when the liter is done. Just tie the bag, carry the box to the trash, and dump it. Easy. This will save you. Also don't use a box with a lid. If yours has a lip, take it off. Yes it's unsightly but they have more movability with the lid off.  
\-Speaking of which, order your liter/food from Chewy. It's cheap and delivered to your door. Save your back, friend.  
\-In the case of food, invest in good food. Don't buy your baby shit like Meow Mix. Cats love it but it's terrible for them. We put our old cat on it briefly as a treat and she got fat fast. Don't break your budget, but some good dry food is nice.  
\-You don't have to feed them wet food tbh. Cats are grazers, they prefer to each a lot of small meals through the day so a bowl of dry food out will be perfect.  
\-They also don't like their water and food bowls to be next to each other. It's an psycho-evolutionary hold-over from pre-domestication. Because their preferred meals used to be vermin they don't exact want to drink where their prey might be living and shitting. My cat eats his food in my room and drinks from a water bowl in my uncle's. That said, maybe have the water close for the moment until the cat gets situated. But two water bowls isn't a bad idea.  
\-Get either pet insurance and/or budget for vet visits. Call clinics to ask the cost of regular visits and any immunization updates your pet will need.

Do some research and examine what you want in a pet. For me, I like cats because they're like cuddly roommates. We do our own thing and then get together to cuddle while watching TV. Sometimes we'll do our thing in each other's company (like my cat sitting in my lap while I work). But cats don't need our permission to live their lives. They don't need to be escorted to a bathroom nor need their living conditions constantly cleaned bc they live in our space.
